_comment: Reviewed exemptions for datrix/scripts/test/ignored-source-gate.ps1.
The gate compares, per framework repo, the working tree against what a
'git add -A' would stage. Anything present on disk that git refuses to
stage is a candidate publishable file being silently deleted by a
.gitignore rule -- unless it is deliberate build output, which is what
this file records.
Each entry excuses ONE .gitignore rule -- identified by the .gitignore
file and the pattern text git check-ignore itself reports -- over ONE
path scope. The scope is load-bearing, not decoration: an unanchored
pattern matches at any depth, so an entry for the root 'build/' tree must
not also excuse the same rule swallowing a 'templates/build/' directory
full of source. That is the exact defect class the gate exists to catch,
and a blanket entry would hide it.
repos is a list of repo names, or ["*"] for every framework repo. The
wildcard is what keeps a newly cloned datrix-* package covered with no
edit here: a bytecode cache is a bytecode cache in every package.
path_glob is segment-aware: '**/' spans whole path segments, '**' spans
the remainder, '*' and '?' stay inside one segment.
pinned_count is the reviewed count of len(exemptions). An entry is only
added or removed together with this number, in the same change; the gate
refuses to run when the two disagree.

exemptions.reason: CPython bytecode cache, rewritten on every interpreter run. Never source, never published.
setuptools distribution metadata written into src/ by an editable install; regenerated by the install, never authored.
PEP 517 / setuptools build tree at the repo root, produced by a wheel or sdist build.
tree-sitter CLI build output beside the grammar. Scoped to this one path because the rule that hides it is unanchored: any other 'build' directory under src/ is a shadowed-source finding, not this.
wheel and sdist output directory produced by a package build.
coverage.py HTML report, regenerated by a coverage run.
coverage.py XML report, regenerated by a coverage run.

coverage.py's own SQLite measurement database, written at the repo root by any run with coverage enabled and rewritten by the next one. Scoped to the root filename only: the sibling entries cover the rendered coverage.xml and htmlcov/ reports, and this is the raw data behind them. It appears and disappears with test activity rather than with authorship, which is why a clean-tree baseline can pass without it and a post-test-run tree cannot.
pytest's own cache of the last run's node IDs and durations.
ruff's incremental lint cache.
Hypothesis example database written during property-based test runs.

import-linter (Grimp) cache directory. The tool writes its own nested .gitignore containing a bare '*', so the responsible rule is that nested file rather than the repo's own .gitignore; the scope keeps the bare wildcard from excusing anything outside the cache.
machine-local task files, developed independently on more than one machine and deliberately never published.
timestamped run artifacts written by the repo test runner (logs, JUnit XML, index.json).
locally regenerated snapshot of the package's directory layout; derived from the tree it describes.
generator state (schema snapshots and migration ledgers) written under a test fixture by a generation run. Scoped to tests/ so the same rule shadowing a .datrix directory under src/ stays a finding.
run and crash logs dropped at the repo root by build and test tooling (JVM hs_err/replay dumps among them). Scoped to the root: a .log file inside a source tree is a finding.
runtime state written by the versioned agent hooks; per-machine, never part of the hook definitions themselves.
machine-local agent permission grants. Deliberately unpublished: the grants record literal local commands and paths, which is a known leak path for customer-specific names.
npm-installed dependency tree, restored from the lockfile; never authored and never published.
TypeScript compiler output for the VS Code client, produced from src/ by the package's own build script.

tree-sitter generated parser source, produced at build time from grammar.js and documented as a generated build artifact in the package manifest. Hidden by an anchored, single-path rule, so it excuses exactly this file.
tree-sitter generated grammar description, produced at build time from grammar.js and documented as a generated build artifact in the package manifest.
tree-sitter generated node-type description, produced at build time from grammar.js and documented as a generated build artifact in the package manifest.
